task:
Write Python 3 function solve(rows). Before the main rule, perform this audit scan in ORIGINAL zero-based order. For an integer row its weight is that integer. For a log-string row its weight is the signed integer between pipes. For a list row its weight is the sum of integer fields excluding booleans plus the lengths of all string fields. Start state at 5. Keep a row if (state + weight + original_index) modulo 7 is not 2, or if it is the last original row. After deciding, update state for EVERY row, including omitted rows: reset to 5 if its weight is zero; otherwise set state to (5*state + weight) modulo 7. Finally rotate the kept list LEFT by final_state modulo kept_length; empty stays empty. Then apply the following main rule: Rows are integer event times. Sort and deduplicate them. A new session begins only when the gap is GREATER than 9. Return sessions as [first,last,count]. Empty input returns [].
Return the requested value, without printing. Inputs follow the types specified. Do not mutate the input. The execution environment permits built-ins and these standard-library modules: math, decimal, fractions, collections, itertools, functools, datetime, calendar, re, statistics, bisect, heapq, operator, string, typing, copy, json, ast, dataclasses, numbers and unicodedata. No file/network I/O is needed.
